analysis_md:
# MTZ — MasTec, Inc.
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-16. Market cap $15.007B at $190.70 (nasdaq_quote_api) — in scope under $40B. All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, fundamentals.json or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Diversified infrastructure contractor (SIC 1623: water, sewer, pipeline, communications and power-line construction) in four segments: Communications, Clean Energy & Infrastructure, Power Delivery, and Pipeline Infrastructure. Revenue FY2025 $14,299,171,000, +16.22% YoY. Q2 2026 set records per the company's release (search result): revenue +23% YoY, 18-month backlog a record $21.4B (+30% YoY, Clean Energy backlog +58%), and management raised FY2026 guidance to $18.2B revenue / $9.30 adjusted EPS — growth of 27% / 42% — helped by The Superior Group acquisition (data-center electrical contractor, ~3,000 employees, closed July 2026; reported $1.65B price, debt-financed, with most of its backlog contribution expected in 2027).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $545,714,000; capex $259,985,000; SBC $34,002,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $251,727,000 = $3.20/share** (latest FY OE/share, key_numbers.md)
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $157,081,000 — below the conservative figure, because FY2025 carried a $409,076,000 working-capital build as revenue accelerated.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years, but violently uneven per share: $8.09 (2021), $0.81 (2022), $5.95 (2023), $11.92 (2024), $3.20 (2025) — the series is dominated by working-capital swings, not by the underlying contracting earnings.
- Net debt $1,934,653,000 plus lease liabilities $468,488,000 (dcf_numbers.json) — and that is the pre-Superior balance sheet; the July 2026 acquisition was financed with cash, credit lines and term loans (company release, via search), so forward leverage is higher than the FY2025 snapshot. No dividend; buybacks $0 TTM (fundamentals.json).

**Base used = normalized 3-yr median OE/share = $5.95** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share, key_numbers.md). The median spans the WC-release-inflated 2024 ($11.92) and the WC-build-depressed 2025 ($3.20) and lands on the 2023 print — it is the engine's designed answer to this filer's OE volatility, and no single year in the series is trustworthy on its own.

**TTM check (ttm.py, filing-direct, run for STALE_FY — saved to ttm.json, quoted in full, NOT used as the base):**
- OCF: FY $545,714,000 − prior YTD $84,011,000 + current YTD $120,322,000 = **TTM $582,025,000**
- Capex: FY $259,985,000 − prior YTD $111,076,000 + current YTD $188,312,000 = **TTM $337,221,000**
- SBC: FY $34,002,000 − prior YTD $16,314,000 + current YTD $19,750,000 = **TTM $37,438,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **78,808,000**
- **TTM OE total $207,366,000 → TTM OE/share $2.63** (fundamentals.json TTM section agrees: OE/share $2.63, OE −65.3% YoY, OCF −30.2% YoY on TTM revenue +23.5% YoY)
- The TTM figure was not adopted: it is another single noisy year, this one carrying a growth-capex surge (TTM capex $337M vs $260M in FY2025) and the working-capital build of a backlog growing 30%. It is disclosed as bear-side evidence — on a TTM base the valuation would print materially lower still. The verdict does not depend on the base choice: even the super-bull scenario on the generous median base values the stock below the price (see table).

## Moat: 4/10 — weak-moderate
Justification: scale, national footprint, bonding capacity, utility/telecom incumbency and a record backlog give real bidding advantages on large programs, but the work is competitively bid, labor- and fleet-based, with thin margins and no durable pricing power. Return evidence (fundamentals.json): roic_proxy and gross margin are null — the filer does not tag the lines those series need — so the computed return series available is ROE: 12.9% (2021), 1.2% (2022), −1.8% (2023), 5.6% (2024), 12.2% (2025), at or below the cost of capital through most of the cycle; FY2025 net margin was 2.79%. Management itself noted on the Q4 2025 call (search result) that ROIC met its WACC hurdle in 2025 for the first time since 2021.
- FOR: scale and national footprint — one of the few contractors that can execute large multi-region power, pipeline, clean-energy and communications programs; record 18-month backlog $21.4B at Q2 2026 (+30% YoY, ~1.2x book-to-bill) gives unusual revenue visibility for a contractor; incumbency and long relationships with utilities, telecom carriers and energy customers, with bonding and safety record gating large-project bidding; diversified end markets plus data-center exposure via Superior.
- AGAINST: competitively bid, project-based work — no recurring revenue or durable pricing power; returns at/below the cost of capital through most of the cycle with a 2.79% FY2025 net margin; labor- and fleet-intensive cost structure — wage pressure and fixed-price execution flow straight to OE; growth partly bought (serial acquisitions; Superior $1.65B debt-financed) with integration and leverage risk; segment cyclicality (Communications softness from RDOF roll-off and wireline deferrals; pipeline project timing).
- A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 7.2 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-16)
Growth blend 13.78% (components: rev CAGR 5y 17.74%, rev CAGR 3y 13.50%, latest rev YoY 16.22%, OE/share CAGR 2y −26.64%; share count CAGR +1.09%/yr applied as a −1.09pp adjustment to the revenue components). **Sanity check against recent prints:** FY2025 revenue +16.22%, TTM revenue +23.5% YoY (fundamentals.json), Q2 2026 +23%, FY2026 guidance +27% — the headline prints all sit above the 13.8% base start, deliberately: the guided 27% includes the inorganic Superior contribution (closed July 2026, backlog contribution mostly 2027) and peak backlog burn, while the company's own initial FY2026 framing was mid-teens organic growth; 13.8% is the organic-like start. The bull start (18.8%) and super-bull start (25.8%) bracket the guided headline rate, so no scenario start needs to exceed what the company just printed — and the super-bull start carries the 1.25 OE multiplier on top. Probabilities were bear-widened to 15/30/30/15/10 for OE_VOLATILE + HIGH_NET_DEBT (45% on bear-or-worse); OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $190.70.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | 1.8% | 0.75 | Infrastructure cycle turns; WC build and leverage bite; Communications/pipeline stall | $35.56 | 4.82% |
| Bear | 30% | 8.8% | 0.90 | TTM-like OE run-rate persists; capex stays at the $337M TTM level | $55.74 | 6.31% |
| Base | 30% | 13.8% | 1.00 | Organic mid-teens growth decays over the 7.2-yr CAP; OE normalizes at the median | $74.71 | 7.70% |
| Bull | 15% | 18.8% | 1.10 | Backlog converts cleanly; Superior integrates; margins expand as guided | $98.83 | 9.39% |
| Super bull | 10% | 25.8% | 1.25 | Guided 27% growth sustains with operating leverage — still not enough | $144.66 | 12.34% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $73.76 (−61.3% vs price), IV@12% $99.43, IV@10% $128.21, weighted IRR 7.66%, base-case IRR 7.70%**
- **Tier by numbers: D; bear tier D, bull tier D — no TIER_BAND ambiguity.** Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 3.12%, terminal value 20.1% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.07x, net debt 4.13x normalized OE, 9.5 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path): 15% at $73.76 · 20% at $50.87 · 25% at $38.42.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 9.5 months ago): ttm.py was run and its full legs are quoted above (TTM OE/share $2.63, saved to ttm.json). The TTM base was *not* adopted — it is a single WC/capex-noise year like the ones the median exists to normalize; the median base is used and the TTM figure is disclosed as bear-side evidence. Current-quarter strength is reflected in the scenario starts instead.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share range over the last 5 years spans >3x): confirmed in the filed series — $8.09 / $0.81 / $5.95 / $11.92 / $3.20 for 2021–25 (financials_history.csv). Resolution: normalized 3-yr median base, bear weight widened to 45% combined (15/30), and the super-bear case carries the 0.75 OE multiplier. This flag is the business: contracting cash flow is a working-capital story year to year.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income and OCF differ by >40% in 2023, 2024): explained from the filed history — it is D&A plus working capital, not an earnings-quality one-off. 2023: net income −$49,949,000 vs OCF $687,277,000 with D&A of $603,200,000 and a $385,025,000 working-capital release. 2024: net income $162,788,000 vs OCF $1,121,625,000 with D&A of $506,600,000 and a further $354,545,000 release. A fleet- and acquisition-heavy contractor mechanically runs OCF far above NI; the OCF-based conservative OE is the right series and is unaffected by the non-cash gap. The same WC swings are what whipsaw OE/share (see OE_VOLATILE).
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY OE/share $3.20 vs 3-yr median $5.95): both are distorted, in opposite directions — 2025 is depressed by the $409,076,000 WC build and $259,985,000 capex of a growth year; the median is pulled up by 2024's WC-release year ($11.92) sitting in the window. The median is the least-bad normalized choice and is used; the latest FY and the TTM ($2.63) are both disclosed, and the verdict survives on any of them because even the super-bull IV on the median base is below the price.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV is 4.07x super-bear IV): real — at a 3.12% OE yield, plausible growth paths fan out. Confidence is low, never high. The spread does not straddle the hurdle: every scenario, including super-bull ($144.66), is below the $190.70 price, so there is no tier ambiguity to size around.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 4.13x normalized OE): stated from the filing — net debt $1,934,653,000 plus lease liabilities $468,488,000 at FY2025 (dcf_numbers.json), against normalized OE of $5.95/share. The bear cases were stressed accordingly (45% bear-or-worse weight), and the FY2025 snapshot *understates* forward leverage: the $1.65B Superior acquisition closed in July 2026 financed with cash, revolver and term loans (company release via search), with management framing pro-forma leverage above the reported 1.8x EBITDA leverage at Q2. Levered OE at 4x+ can vanish fast in a downturn — that is the super-bear story.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The market is paying for the backlog and the guidance — $21.4B backlog, +27% guided revenue, +42% guided adjusted EPS — at $190.70. The owner's-earnings record says the cash conversion of that growth is the weak link: TTM OE/share *fell* to $2.63 on TTM revenue of $16,109,103,000 (fundamentals.json) because growth consumes working capital and fleet capex before it pays. Adjusted EPS and OE are telling opposite stories, and the sweep prices OE.
- Method range: the base choice moves the IV a lot (median $5.95 vs TTM $2.63 is a >2x base gap) but not the tier — on the most generous base, even the super-bull case (25.8% start, 1.25x OE) reaches only $144.66 at a 15% discount, 12.34% IRR. There is no defensible pass-1 method that gets MTZ to Tier C at this price.
- What would change the answer: two or three years of OE conversion at the guided EBITDA margins — i.e., the 2024-style combination of growth *without* a WC build — or a price near $74. Watch H2 2026 OCF (Q4 is seasonally dominant), Superior integration, and whether pro-forma leverage comes back under the company's stated policy by year-end as management guided.

## Data notes
Enrichment (step 9) all ran: fundamentals.json, prices.json, segments.json, statements.json, profile.json / street.json, live.json written. One non-blocking warning: profile.py found no 10-K Item 1 Business section outside the table of contents (10-K filed 2026-02-26), so profile.json's description is null — the company page's About text is missing, nothing in the score depends on it. statements.py also flagged a filer's sign slip in a 2014-period investing line (PaymentsToAcquireOtherInvestments filed negative), read as the absolute amount paid; it does not touch any year in the OE history used here.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 7.66% on the normalized median base; bear and bull tiers both D)
- Confidence: **Low** (OE volatility 0.81–11.92/share over five years, 4.07x scenario spread, leverage rising post-period — but the D itself is robust: no scenario on the most generous base clears even 13%)
- One-liner: Diversified infrastructure contractor with a record backlog but a weak 4/10 moat and volatile, working-capital-driven owner's earnings — at $190.70 it clears nothing: weighted IRR 7.7%, weighted IV@15% $73.76, and even the super-bull IV@15% ($144.66) sits below price; it would need ~$74 to clear 15%.
